Building metrics from fresh NCCS downloads

Source: vignettes/build-from-nccs.Rmd
build-from-nccs.Rmd

You don’t need the SOI panel to build metrics. With source = "nccs", npcompete downloads the public files of the National Center for Charitable Statistics (NCCS) and harmonizes them to the archive’s layout. It caches the result, so later builds work offline. Every metric and option in vignette("build-from-archive") works the same way.

The downloads need an internet connection and the arrow package. The code chunks in this article are shown with output from a real run (tax years 2018 and 2019) rather than run when the article is built.

library( npcompete )

What gets downloaded

Live builds use two NCCS products:

File What it supplies Size
CORE 990combined, one Parquet file per year (processed_merged/core/{Y}/990combined/) Form 990 and 990-EZ financials for every subsection: revenue, expenses, assets, liabilities, net assets, program revenue, contributions, investment income about 50 MB a year, 2010 onward
Unified geocoded BMF (geocoding/unified-bmf/latest/) One record per EIN: geocoded county, NTEEV2 subsector, ruling date about 640 MB, once

Each CORE file holds the returns whose fiscal year ended in that calendar year. npcompete uses the SOI convention for tax years: tax year t is the year the fiscal year began. Returns for years ending in December come from file t, and returns for years ending in any other month come from file t + 1. Building tax year 2019 therefore downloads the 2019 and 2020 files. A tax year whose t + 1 file is still partial is flagged as incomplete.

Where the downloads go

Files are cached under npc_cache_dir(). By default this is the user cache folder that tools::R_user_dir() returns. Choose another folder with options(npcompete.cache_dir = ) or the NPCOMPETE_CACHE environment variable.

npc_cache_dir()
#> [1] "C:\\Users\\jlecy\\AppData\\Local/R/cache/R/npcompete"
options( npcompete.cache_dir = "D:/data/npcompete-nccs" )

Build metrics in one call

npc_build_metrics() builds any tax years it needs that are not in the cache yet, then computes the metrics:

m <- npc_build_metrics( 2018:2019, geo = "cbsa",
                        resources = c( "TOTREV", "NETASS" ),
                        source = "nccs" )
#> Building tax year(s) 2018, 2019 from NCCS downloads into D:/data/npcompete-nccs ...
#> Downloading https://nccsdata.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/geocoding/unified-bmf/latest/bmf_unified_geocoded.parquet ...
#> Reading the unified BMF ...
#> Downloading https://nccsdata.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/processed_merged/core/2018/990combined/core_2018_990combined.parquet ...
#> Downloading https://nccsdata.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/processed_merged/core/2019/990combined/core_2019_990combined.parquet ...
#> Downloading https://nccsdata.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/processed_merged/core/2020/990combined/core_2020_990combined.parquet ...
#> Harmonizing 1,580,115 CORE rows ...
#> Done: 1,047,660 rows for tax years 2018-2019.
#> Reading 2 year(s) from the NCCS build ...
#> Building cbsa metrics for TOTREV ...
#> Building cbsa metrics for NETASS ...

The first run downloads about 0.8 GB and takes a few minutes. Later runs for the same years read only the cache.

Or build the organization table first

npc_build_nccs() downloads and harmonizes the requested years without computing metrics. It keeps years already built, so the table can grow a few years at a time:

npc_build_nccs( 2015:2022 )

A live build has the same layout as the archive, so npc_archive_info() and npc_get_orgs() work on it. Its year counts also record the CORE files and the BMF version used for each tax year:

npc_archive_info( npc_cache_dir() )$year_counts
#>   YEAR      N SHARE_OF_MEDIAN INCOMPLETE
#> 1 2018 524647           1.002      FALSE
#> 2 2019 523013           0.998      FALSE

These counts include every subsection. npc_get_orgs() keeps 501(c)(3) organizations by default:

orgs <- npc_get_orgs( 2019, source = "nccs" )
head( orgs[ c( "EIN2", "YEAR", "COUNTY_FIPS", "CBSA_FIPS", "NTEEV2",
               "FILER_TYPE", "TOTREV" ) ] )
#>             EIN2 YEAR COUNTY_FIPS CBSA_FIPS     NTEEV2 FILER_TYPE   TOTREV
#> 1 EIN-01-0011694 2019       25009     14460 PSB-S00-NS      990EZ     8332
#> 2 EIN-01-0015091 2019       34027     35620 HMS-N64-RG      990EZ   113339
#> 3 EIN-01-0017496 2019       23031     38860 UNU-Z99-RG      990EZ   152931
#> 4 EIN-01-0024645 2019       23019     12620 ART-A69-RG        990  1084597
#> 5 EIN-01-0032215 2019       23015      <NA> UNU-Z99-RG        990     1405
#> 6 EIN-01-0130427 2019       23005     38860 HOS-E22-RG        990 49375323

CBSA_FIPS is NA for counties outside every metro and micro area.

Reproducibility

Every downloaded file is logged in downloads.csv in the cache, with its URL, size, MD5 hash and download time. The year counts record which CORE files and which BMF (by hash and vintage) went into each tax year. The metrics manifest (attr(m, "manifest"), or manifest.csv when you set out_dir) records the source and options.

NCCS updates its files, and the BMF in particular is replaced every month. A cached build does not change until you ask:

npc_build_nccs( 2018:2019, refresh = TRUE )   # download again and rebuild

A cache folder is a frozen build. Copy it, or build straight into a project folder with npc_build_nccs( years, dir = "..." ). Then pass the folder as dir to npc_build_metrics( ..., source = "nccs" ) to rebuild the same tables later.

How live builds differ from the archive

County comes from the current address. The unified BMF has one record per EIN, so an organization that moved is placed at its latest address in every year. The archive geocodes each year’s filing.

Counties are matched by name. The BMF geocodes give county and state names but not FIPS codes. npc_match_county() matches them to the counties in pop_county, handling parishes, boroughs, census areas and independent cities:

npc_match_county( c( "Cook County", "City of Baltimore", "Baltimore County",
                     "Lafourche Parish", "Municipality of Anchorage" ),
                  c( "IL", "MD", "MD", "LA", "AK" ) )
#> [1] "17031" "24510" "24005" "22057" "02020"

About 0.2% of filers end up without a county, usually because they have no usable address.

Some fields are missing. The CORE 990combined files have no professional fundraising fees, so FNDFEE is NA and the FUNDRAISER_SHARE and FUNDRAISING_RATIO metrics are empty. Revocation dates are also NA, as is the geocoded CBSA, so use the default cbsa = "crosswalk".

Net assets for 990-EZ filers are total assets minus total liabilities, as in the SOI panel. The net assets line on the 990-EZ often disagrees with the balance sheet.

Checking a live build against the archive

If you also have the archive, npc_compare_sources() reads the same years from both and reports where they agree:

cmp <- npc_compare_sources( 2018:2019,
                            archive_dir = npc_archive_dir(),
                            nccs_dir    = npc_cache_dir() )
cmp$totals[ c( "YEAR", "SOURCE", "N", "TOTREV", "NETASS" ) ]
#>   YEAR  SOURCE      N       TOTREV       NETASS
#> 1 2018 archive 398437 2.388472e+12 2.877826e+12
#> 2 2018    nccs 398434 2.388471e+12 2.877825e+12
#> 3 2019 archive 399848 2.502469e+12 3.029709e+12
#> 4 2019    nccs 399844 2.502468e+12 3.029709e+12
cmp$ein_match[ c( "YEAR", "BOTH", "ARCHIVE_ONLY", "NCCS_ONLY", "SAME_COUNTY",
                  "SAME_TOTREV", "SAME_NETASS" ) ]
#>   YEAR   BOTH ARCHIVE_ONLY NCCS_ONLY SAME_COUNTY SAME_TOTREV SAME_NETASS
#> 1 2018 398434            3         0   0.9600780   1.0000000   0.9988656
#> 2 2019 399844            4         0   0.9588233   0.9999975   0.9991747
cmp$market_summary
#>   YEAR MARKETS     COR_N MEDIAN_ABS_PCT_DIFF
#> 1 2018    2392 0.9998691            2.241597
#> 2 2019    2397 0.9998682            2.173913

The two sources hold the same 501(c)(3) filers, apart from three or four a year, and identical financial values for virtually all of them. Organization counts by county correlate at 0.9999. The median county differs by about 2%, almost all of it from the address difference described above. data-raw/validate-nccs-source.R in the package repository runs this check for any years.
